summary:
I brought the TS prototype into line with all twelve §9 rulings except K8, which can't be met on Bun and is recorded as a stack limitation. All four targets build (exit 0); the 153 native tests pass against both the source and the darwin-arm64 binary (exit 0 both). The evidence record is "verified" with verdict "fail" (because of K8). Native Windows runs are blocked: no Windows x64 host.

| Ruling | Result | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| K1 | Changed. Control characters (C0 incl. TAB, DEL, C1) and invalid UTF-8 in `comment` and `key_type` now become U+FFFD instead of `\u001b`-style text. A `key_type` that is not valid UTF-8 now gives U+FFFD, not a protocol error. Files: `src/domain/result.ts`, `src/domain/agent.ts`. | Three K1 tests in `agent.test.ts`, one of them end-to-end through a fake agent socket |
| K2 | Changed. A control character in a profile string value outside `[meta]` gives `SCHEMA_INVALID`; `key_path` names the key and the value is never echoed. File: `src/domain/profile.ts`. | Six domain tests, one CLI test and one `[meta]`-tolerance test in `profile.test.ts` |
| K3 | Already conformed | New close and reset tests in `agent.test.ts` |
| K4 | Already conformed | Existing domain test plus a new end-to-end test |
| K5 | Already conformed | `run.test.ts` now asserts `state` |
| K6 | Changed (see below) | Three tests in `run.test.ts`, the probe script, and both Linux containers |
| K7 | Statement only | — |
| K8 | Stack limitation | `61 ff 62` arrives as `61 ef bf bd 62` on macOS and both Linux containers. No workaround added. |
| K9 | Changed. Each filter edit (append, Backspace, Esc) selects the first shown row; Enter keeps the selection. File: `src/domain/listview.ts`. | Unit test plus an assertion in the real-PTY filter test |
| K10 | Already conformed | Added "no SELECTED output" checks and a terminal-hangup test (exit 129) |
| K11 | Changed (see below) | Five tests in the new `test/dist.test.ts`, the probe script, and both Linux containers |
| K12 | Statement only | — |

**K6.** The fix needed about 170 lines of unsafe `bun:ffi` code in a new `src/platform/posix-spawn.ts`, because `Bun.spawn` can't put the child in its own process group.
- **How it works.** The child is launched with `posix_spawnp` in its own process group, with default signal handling and no leaked file descriptors. When `heimdall-proto` is the terminal's foreground group, it hands the terminal to the child and takes it back afterwards. Every signal it receives is forwarded exactly once.
- **Proof.** An explicit `kill -INT` while `heimdall-proto` is in the foreground now reaches the child once; the old build delivered it 0 times.
- **Old double-delivery.** The old build also delivered a terminal resize (SIGWINCH) twice; that is fixed.
- **Launch-failure pre-check.** I added a `Bun.which` lookup before spawning. Without it, the emulated linux-x64 container reported a missing command as a normal exit 127.
- **Ctrl-Z.** I added handling so it doesn't leave the terminal owned by a stopped child.

**K11.** `build.sh` no longer embeds the OpenTUI library.
- **Sidecar layout.** It ships the library as `dist/<target>/@opentui/core-<platform>/<lib>`. Each target's library is listed under `sidecars` in `dist/manifest.json`.
- **Loading.** The program loads it only from its own real directory and overrides inherited `OTUI_ASSET_ROOT` and `OPENTUI_LIBC`. If the sidecar is missing, the TUI exits 1 with no fallback.
- **TMPDIR.** A fresh empty TMPDIR stays empty for every command, on macOS and in both Linux containers.
- **Still open.** `BUN_BE_BUN=1` still turns the binary into a general Bun runtime. No build flag disables it, so it is recorded as a stack limitation.

**Negative control.** I ran the new suite against a binary rebuilt from the old sources. It failed 9 tests, exactly on the changed behaviors; the K3, K4 and K10 tests passed, as expected for already-conformed rulings.

**Shared harness.** An informational, read-only run scored 95/95. That harness version still treats the invalid-UTF-8 argv check as non-gating (contrary to K8); the check itself recorded the mismatch.

**Other updates.** I appended the "§9 alignment (2026-10-03)" section to `REPORT.md` and marked the statements it made stale. I also corrected `LICENSES.md`: judging by the size drop, the old Linux binaries embedded the musl library as well as the glibc one.

**Decisions for you:**
- **E1.** The sidecar sits in a subdirectory of the executable's directory, because OpenTUI's lookup path forces it. A flat layout would need a patched OpenTUI. Does that count as "its own directory" under K11?
- **E2.** The raw argv bytes are reachable through `bun:ffi` and could be passed to the spawn call K6 already uses, which would fix K8. I didn't do it because K8 says not to route around a stack limitation; does `bun:ffi` count as "the stack"?
- **E3.** The harness owner should make the argv check gating to match K8.
- **E4.** The Ctrl-Z handling (about 10 lines, own test) goes beyond §9; keep it or drop it.
